extent:
Four bodies of law, on four lines that never rejoin, from Gratian to 2023.

WHAT IS HERE. The classical Corpus Iuris Canonici as six stations, of which
three carry a promulgating bull whose text was read and three claim no act at
all. The 1917 Pio-Benedictine Code, whose Latin is public domain and is printed
here for the canons this record carries. The 1983 Code with the twelve acts that
have amended it and the fourteen occasions on which the Pope disposed of an
authentic interpretation of it. The 1990 Code of Canons of the Eastern Churches,
with the four motu proprios of Pius XII that partly codified Eastern law before
it and the six acts that have since amended it.

WHAT IS NOT HERE, AND WHY.

No text of the 1983 Code, of the CCEO, or of any act amending either. Those
canons stand with their number, their paragraph, their place in the structure,
every act that established or changed them, and a stated reason where the words
would be. That is a rights position and not ignorance, and the two are drawn
differently everywhere.

No text of any canon of the Corpus Iuris Canonici. Those three lines carry
stations, witnesses and descent, and no law. The Decretum alone runs to some
3,800 chapters; transcribing any part of it is a different lane's work, and
until it is done a query about what two lines share can report acts and cannot
report text.

Not every canon of any of these Codes. This record carries a canon when an act
touched it, when an authentic interpretation was given on it, when this
repository already held a verified reading of it, or when it is the canon the
whole apparatus is built to answer a question about. Counted at the tips: 86
canons of the 1983 Code in 99 base units, 39 of the Eastern Code in 45, and 12
of the 1917 Code in 25. The 1983 Code has 1752 canons, so this is five per cent
of one Code and a smaller fraction of the others.

Not the whole of Book VI of the 1983 Code. Pascite gregem Dei substituted the
entire Book -- cann. 1311-1399, eighty-nine canons, confirmed by counting the
canon numbers in the Latin PDF the Holy See serves -- and this record carries
the five of them that some other act or interpretation independently reaches. So
that station's diff is five canons wide and the act was eighty-nine wide, and
saying so here is the only way the difference does not read as a claim.

lines.label: The Corpus Iuris Canonici
lines.note:
The classical law: Gratian's concordance and the four papal collections that
grew around it, gathered and corrected by order of Gregory XIII in 1582 and in
force until the 1917 Code abrogated it. Six stations, no unit of law
transcribed, and four of the six standing as roots because no instrument was
found that says what any of them follows.

lines.label: The Pio-Benedictine Code (1917)
lines.note:
The first codification of Latin canon law, begun under Pius X, promulgated by
Benedict XV on 27 May 1917 and in force from 19 May 1918 until the 1983 Code
took effect. This is the only body of law in this record whose words may be
printed here, and they are.

lines.label: The Code of 1983
lines.note:
The Code now in force for the Latin Church, with every act that has amended it
and every occasion on which the Pope disposed of an authentic interpretation of
it. It is the one line here that descends from another: Sacrae disciplinae leges
recounts the announcement of a reform of the Code of 1917, and 1983 c. 6 §1 1°
abrogates that Code by name.

lines.label: The Code of Canons of the Eastern Churches (1990)
lines.note:
Eastern law, codified in part by four motu proprios of Pius XII between 1949 and
1957 and wholly by John Paul II in 1990. It is a line of its own and never
rejoins the Latin one. A whole-file search of the CCEO's three Latin deliveries
for `Codicis Iuris Canonici` returns 0; the Latin Church appears in it ten times
and every one of them is in the form `of any Church sui iuris, the Latin Church
included`.

stations.effect:
Every canon of the 1917 Code leaves this record's law at this station, and the

Titles II, III, IV, V and XVII of the draft -- the largest of the four, running

stations.effect:
The sharpest of the three, and the reason a canon lawyer looks these up:
outside danger of death, the power to dispense in c. 87 §1 does not reach the
canonical form of marriage between two Catholics. The canon is not changed by a
syllable and its reach is settled.

stations.effect:
The correctores Romani did not restore the Decretum as Gratian composed it.
Friedberg says as much of them in terms: their aim was not to restore the text
as Gratian had made it but as Gratian ought to have made it.
stations.instrument: Breve Emendationem decretorum

One of the four settles the reach of c. 1673 3°, which Mitis Iudex substituted
twenty-nine years later. A reader following that canon sees an interpretation
that answered a question about a text that no longer stands.

The Eastern twin of Mitis Iudex, issued the same day and drawn as its own

stations.title: Abortion in c. 1398 is settled to mean more than the expulsion of a fetus

stations.effect: Canons 435 §1 and 506 §1 are reissued. In force from 8 December 2020.

stations.title: Ab initio changes two canons on Eastern religious

stations.authority: John Paul II, ordering the decision made public

stations.effect:
Canon 489 §2 extends an indult of exclaustration from three years to five; c.
496 is reissued and its §2 DELETED; cann. 499, 501 §2, 546 §2 and 552 §1 move
decisions about dismissal and departure; cann. 1052 and 1054 move the reduction

stations.instrument: Litterae apostolicae motu proprio datae Competentias quasdam decernere
stations.title: Competentias quasdam decernere moves eight Eastern competences down from Rome

stations.authority: John Paul II, disposing in audience of a decision of the pontifical body charged with the authentic interpretation of the Code

stations.title: Two doubts answered: a chapter of canons, and a diocesan tax

stations.effect:
The Eastern counterpart of Pascite gregem Dei, and the act says so: it recites
that the Latin penal canons were changed by that constitution of 23 May 2021 and
then reforms twenty-two canons of Title XXVII of the Eastern Code together with
can. 1152. In force from 29 June 2023.
stations.instrument: Litterae apostolicae motu proprio datae Vocare peccatores
stations.title: Vocare peccatores reforms the Eastern penal law

stations.authority: John Paul II, disposing in audience of a decision of the pontifical body charged with the authentic interpretation of the Code
stations.citation: AAS 82 (1990) 845, as reproduced in the Holy See's Latin collection Interpretationes Authenticae, sha256 1e7a0aaa...
stations.instrument: Responsum ad propositum dubium, coetus plenarius 8 Maii 1990 (Pastor bonus art. 154)
stations.title: An absolute majority is still required at the third scrutiny

stations.effect:
Canon 102 gains a new §3 -- with the old §3 renumbered §4 -- and cann. 66 §1, 149
and 183 §1 are reissued so as to keep it in view. In force one month after
publication in L'Osservatore Romano.
stations.instrument: Litterae apostolicae motu proprio datae Iam pridem
stations.title: Iam pridem sets an age at which an Eastern bishop loses his vote

stations.authority: John Paul II, confirming the decision and ordering it promulgated

stations.title: Two doubts on the synod of bishops and on a diocesan bishop

stations.authority: John Paul II, confirming the decision and ordering it promulgated

stations.instrument: Responsum ad propositum dubium, coetus plenarius 30 Iunii 1992 (Pastor bonus art. 154)
stations.title: Service at the altar is held to be among the offices c. 230 §2 opens to lay people

stations.citation: Ioannes Paulus II, m.p. Ad tuendam fidem, 18 Maii 1998; Latin delivery on vatican.va, sha256 ce72ecd8..., carrying `© Copyright 1998 - Libreria Editrice Vaticana`.
stations.effect:
The middle clause of the Profession of Faith -- on truths definitively proposed
by the Magisterium concerning faith or morals -- had no corresponding canon in
either Code, and the motu proprio says so in terms and fills the gap. Canon 750
gains a second paragraph, its existing text becoming §1; canon 1371 n. 1 gains a
reference to the new §2 beside the reference to c. 752 it already carried. The
Eastern Code is amended in the same document and in the same way.
stations.instrument: Litterae apostolicae motu proprio datae Ad tuendam fidem
stations.title: Ad tuendam fidem inserts the second clause of the Profession of Faith into both Codes

stations.authority: John Paul II, confirming the decision and ordering it promulgated
stations.citation: AAS 90 (1998) 711, as reproduced in the Holy See's Latin collection Interpretationes Authenticae, sha256 1e7a0aaa...
stations.instrument: Responsum ad propositum dubium, coetus ordinarius 16 Iunii 1998 (Pastor bonus art. 154)
stations.title: A confessor may require the fixed grille even when the penitent asks otherwise

stations.authority: John Paul II, confirming the decision and ordering it promulgated
stations.citation: AAS 91 (1999) 918, as reproduced in the Holy See's Latin collection Interpretationes Authenticae, sha256 1e7a0aaa...
stations.effect:
The answer is `Negative et ad mentem`, and the mind is then stated: any action
voluntarily and gravely despising the sacred species is included in the word.
This is the one entry in the whole collection whose President appended a
commentary, in Italian and in English, and it is the ONLY PLACE ANYWHERE IN THE
COLLECTION where c. 16 §2 is cited at all -- and even there it is cited for the
fact that the Holy Father confirmed the decision and ordered its promulgation,
not to name which of the four species of interpretation this one is.
stations.instrument: Responsum ad propositum dubium, coetus ordinarius 4 Iunii 1999 (Pastor bonus art. 154)
stations.title: To throw away the sacred species is settled to mean more than throwing

stations.citation: Benedictus XVI, m.p. Omnium in mentem, 26 Octobris 2009; Latin delivery on vatican.va, carrying `© Copyright 2009 - Libreria Editrice Vaticana`.
stations.effect:
Five articles and two subjects. Articles 1 and 2 change cann. 1008 and 1009 so
that the Code says of bishops and priests that they act in the person of Christ
the Head and of deacons that they serve the people of God -- the motu proprio
says it is following a change John Paul II had already ordered in n. 875 of the
Catechism. Articles 3 to 5 strike the words about defection by a formal act from
cann. 1086 §1, 1117 and 1124, so that a baptized Catholic is bound by the
canonical form of marriage and by the impediment of disparity of worship
whatever he has since declared. The motu proprio's own account of why is
unusually blunt: the exception had proved impossible to determine in practice,
had operated as an inducement to apostasy where Catholics were few, and had left
many marriages clandestine.
stations.instrument: Litterae apostolicae motu proprio datae Omnium in mentem
stations.title: Omnium in mentem changes what the diaconate is said to do, and abolishes the formal act of defection

stations.citation: Franciscus, m.p. Mitis Iudex Dominus Iesus, 15 Augusti 2015; Latin delivery on vatican.va, sha256 recorded on its witness row.
stations.effect:
Twenty-one canons substituted at once, and THE CANON A READER USUALLY ARRIVES
WITH IS NOT AMONG THEM. The act decrees that Book VII, Part III, Title I, Chapter
I of the Code, on cases for declaring the nullity of a marriage, cann. 1671 to
1691, be SUBSTITUTED ENTIRE from 8 December 2015 -- and it then prints the new
chapter, in seven articles. What it changes is the process: a single conforming
sentence is no longer required, the diocesan bishop is himself the judge, a
shorter process before the bishop is created for cases of manifest nullity,
appeal goes to the metropolitan see, and the tribunals are to be made free of
charge where an episcopal conference can manage it. It changes nothing about
what makes a marriage null. Canon 1095, on incapacity to consent, is untouched
by it and by every other act in this record: it stands in this record exactly as
Sacrae disciplinae leges left it in 1983.
stations.instrument: Litterae apostolicae motu proprio datae Mitis Iudex Dominus Iesus
stations.title: Mitis Iudex Dominus Iesus substitutes the whole process for declaring a marriage null

stations.citation: Franciscus, m.p. De concordia inter Codices, 31 Maii 2016; Latin delivery on vatican.va, sha256 af1c1c0c...
stations.effect:
Eleven articles, every one of them amending the LATIN Code and none of them the
Eastern -- which is the finding, because the title is about concord between the
two and the harmonisation runs one way. Canons 111 and 112 are substituted
whole, on which Church sui iuris a person is ascribed to and how he transfers;
c. 535 §2 on what the baptismal register records; c. 868 §1 2° and a new §3 on
the baptism of a child of non-Catholic Christians; a new c. 1108 §3 reserving
valid assistance at a marriage involving an Eastern party to a PRIEST; cann.
1109, 1111 §1 and 1112 §1 in consequence; a new c. 1116 §3; and c. 1127 §1,
which makes canonical form a requirement of lawfulness only, and the priest's
intervention a requirement of validity, where a Catholic marries a non-Catholic
of an Eastern rite.

Its own model is stated: it cites CCEO cann. 40 §3, 193 §1 and 39 as what the
Latin canons are being brought into line with. Six years later Competentias
quasdam decernere does the same thing in miniature, amending Latin c. 265 in so
many words `so that it may better agree with CCEO can. 357 §1`.
stations.instrument: Litterae apostolicae motu proprio datae De concordia inter Codices
stations.title: De concordia inter codices bends eleven Latin canons toward the Eastern Code

stations.authority: Francis, informed of the decision and ordering it published
stations.citation: AAS 108 (2016) 707; the Acta page itself as a PDF from delegumtextibus.va, sha256 416598c0..., and the Latin with an Italian translation in the Holy See press bulletin of 15 September 2016, sha256 10a639f8...
stations.instrument: Responsum ad propositum dubium, coetus plenarius 23 Iunii 2015 (Pastor bonus art. 154)
stations.title: The irregularities of c. 1041 are held to reach the non-Catholic

stations.citation: Franciscus, m.p. Magnum principium, 3 Septembris 2017; Latin delivery on vatican.va.
stations.effect:
Canon 838 is given in full in four paragraphs and replaces the canon of 1983.
The substance is in §§2 and 3: the Apostolic See RECOGNISES adaptations approved
by an episcopal conference, and an episcopal conference prepares and approves
vernacular translations and publishes them AFTER CONFIRMATION by the Apostolic
See. `Recognitio` and `confirmatio` are made two different things done to two
different objects, which is the whole of the change and the reason it was made.
The motu proprio then directs that art. 64 §3 of Pastor bonus and the other laws
about translations be interpreted accordingly.
stations.instrument: Litterae apostolicae motu proprio datae Magnum principium
stations.title: Magnum principium rewrites canon 838 and moves the liturgical translations

stations.citation: Franciscus, m.p. Communis vita, 19 Martii 2019; Latin delivery on vatican.va.
stations.effect:
Canon 694 is substituted whole and gains a third ground of dismissal by the fact
itself -- twelve continuous months of unlawful absence from the religious house,
with the member's untraceability kept in view -- together with a new §3 requiring
the Holy See to confirm the superior's declaration of the fact, or the bishop of
the principal see for an institute of diocesan right. Canon 729, on secular
institutes, is substituted in consequence, and the act says so: the new number
in c. 694 §1 carries with it the change to c. 729, whose reference to the
grounds of dismissal did not include unlawful absence.
stations.instrument: Litterae apostolicae motu proprio datae Communis vita
stations.title: Communis vita makes a year's unlawful absence a dismissal by the fact itself

stations.citation: Franciscus, m.p. Authenticum charismatis, 1 Novembris 2020; Latin delivery on vatican.va.
stations.effect:
Canon 579 is substituted. The change is one word of procedure and a large change
of practice: a diocesan bishop may erect an institute of consecrated life in his
territory only after obtaining the LICENCE of the Apostolic See in writing,
where the canon of 1983 required that he first consult it. The motu proprio's
reason is that such an erection, though it happens in a particular Church, is a
gift to the whole Church and is of great moment for it.
stations.instrument: Litterae apostolicae motu proprio datae Authenticum charismatis
stations.title: Authenticum charismatis requires Roman licence before a bishop erects an institute

stations.citation: Franciscus, m.p. Spiritus Domini, 10 Ianuarii 2021; Latin delivery on vatican.va.
stations.effect:
Canon 230 §1 alone. The canon of 1983 opened the stable ministries of lector and
acolyte to LAY MEN of the age and qualities an episcopal conference decrees; the
substituted text says LAY PEOPLE and changes nothing else, keeping the same
clause that the conferral gives no right to support or remuneration from the
Church. The motu proprio's stated ground is that these ministries rest on
baptism rather than on ordination, and it notes that c. 230 §2 already implied
as much.
stations.instrument: Litterae apostolicae motu proprio datae Spiritus Domini
stations.title: Spiritus Domini opens the instituted ministries of lector and acolyte to women

stations.citation: Franciscus, const. ap. Pascite gregem Dei, 23 Maii 2021; Latin delivery on vatican.va, and the recognised Book VI as a Latin PDF from the Holy See's own Code archive, sha256 20fad041...
stations.effect:
The largest single change to the 1983 Code. The constitution promulgates the
recognised text of Book VI, De sanctionibus poenalibus in Ecclesia, and abrogates
the Book VI of 1983 when the new one takes force -- eighty-nine canons, cann.
1311 to 1399, counted in the Latin text the Holy See serves. It takes force on 8
December 2021, and it is promulgated by publication in L'Osservatore Romano and
only afterwards printed in the Acta.
stations.instrument: Constitutio apostolica Pascite gregem Dei
stations.title: Pascite gregem Dei substitutes the whole of Book VI

stations.citation: Franciscus, m.p. Competentias quasdam decernere, 11 Februarii 2022; Latin delivery on vatican.va, sha256 84968b4c..., served from a path named `assegnare-alcune-competenze`.
stations.effect:
Ten articles moving decisions from the Apostolic See to bishops, episcopal
conferences and major superiors, and in three places replacing APPROVAL by the
Holy See with CONFIRMATION -- for an interdiocesan seminary and its statutes in
c. 237 §2, for a national programme of priestly formation in c. 242 §1, and for
a catechism published by a conference in c. 775 §2. Canon 265 adds public
clerical associations to the structures a cleric may be incardinated in; c. 604
gains a §3 letting a bishop or a conference recognise and erect associations of
virgins; c. 686 §1 extends an indult of exclaustration to five years; cann. 688
§2, 699 §2 and 700 move decisions about departure and dismissal to the supreme
moderator with his council; and cann. 1308 and 1310 move the reduction of Mass
obligations and the commutation of pious wills to the diocesan bishop and the
ordinary.

It amends the Eastern Code in the same document, and stands there as its own
station.
stations.instrument: Litterae apostolicae motu proprio datae Competentias quasdam decernere
stations.title: Competentias quasdam decernere moves eleven Latin competences down from Rome

stations.citation: Franciscus, m.p. Recognitum Librum VI, 26 Aprilis 2022; Latin delivery on vatican.va.
stations.effect:
The smallest act on this line and the clearest illustration of why a
substitution has consequences. Canon 695 §1 requires a religious to be dismissed
for certain delicts, and it named them by canon number. Book VI renumbered the
delicts, so the canon pointed at the wrong ones. The motu proprio's own account
is exactly that: in the recognised Book VI the treatment of certain delicts was
changed, new delicts were introduced, and the numbering of the canons was also
altered, so an adjustment is required for these to agree with the canons of the
other Books. Canon 695 §1 is reissued with the new numbers.
stations.instrument: Litterae apostolicae motu proprio datae Recognitum Librum VI
stations.title: Recognitum Librum VI repairs a cross-reference the new Book VI broke
